deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a draft of the part of Riemann's 1851 Göttingen dissertation (Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse, the articles on the Dirichlet principle) that discusses the functional L. L is the Dirichlet-type integral of λ (in the dissertation, L = ∫∫((∂α/∂x−∂β/∂y)²+(∂α/∂y+∂β/∂x)²) dT). Here λ is required to agree with a prescribed, possibly discontinuous, function g near the discontinuities of g.

(1) Riemann says some earlier articles allowed certain inaccuracies for brevity, and these are now to be removed. He will first justify the restriction in two cases: g discontinuous along a line, or g discontinuous at a point O.

(2) The restriction stated: L must stay finite, so λ cannot approach a discontinuous g arbitrarily closely. Equivalently, suppose λ is required to coincide with g outside a region T' that contains the discontinuities. Then T' can be taken so small that L exceeds any given bound C. What must be shown is that the region T' where λ ≠ g cannot shrink to nothing while L stays bounded.

(3) Line case, set-up. Use coordinates (s, p) near a continuously curved piece of the discontinuity line:
- s is arc length along the line;
- p is signed normal distance;
- κ is the curvature, taken positive when the line is concave toward the side of positive p.

The area element is then dT = (1−κp) dp ds (my fill-in; this is what gives the parallel-curve length factor). Let p1 > 0 and p2 < 0 be the values of p at the boundary of T' on the two sides, and let γ1 = g(s,p1), γ2 = g(s,p2) be the corresponding values of g, where λ = g.

(4) Line case, estimate (completed from the next page; the steps are mine where implicit). For fixed s, the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality gives
(γ1−γ2)² = (∫_{p2}^{p1} λ_p dp)² ≤ ∫ λ_p²(1−κp) dp · ∫ dp/(1−κp).
The second factor is ∫_{p2}^{p1} dp/(1−κp) = (log(1−κp2) − log(1−κp1))/κ. Hence
L ≥ ∫∫_{T'} λ_p² dT ≥ ∫ (γ1−γ2)² κ ds / (log(1−κp2) − log(1−κp1)).
As p1, p2 → 0 the denominator tends to 0. So wherever γ1 ≠ γ2 on a stretch of positive length, the bound blows up: L > C for T' thin enough.

(5) Point case. For isolated discontinuity points of the degree admitted earlier, the remainder of T outside T' (respectively T' itself in the line case) contributes an unboundedly large amount to L. So the restriction is justified.

(6) Refinements:
- L can be made large even if one of p1, p2 is 0, provided T' has finite width on the other side.
- The constant M (m on the next page) need not be the infimum of (γ1−γ2)² over intervals of p1, p2. It suffices that within every δ there exist p1, p2 with (γ1−γ2)² > m.
- This is a limsup-type jump condition. It is needed for oscillating discontinuities such as sin(1/ρ), treated on the next page.
errors: The area element (1−κp) and the bound p1 < 1/κ (so that the logarithms are defined) are left implicit.
The Cauchy–Schwarz step is not written out on this page.
The point-singularity case is only asserted, with no estimate given.
The draft is heavily struck through, and the logic of the last paragraph (p1 or p2 = 0) is fragmentary.
The arguments are not errors, but are standard-of-the-time heuristics: e.g. a uniform positive lower bound for (γ1−γ2)² along a set of s of positive length is tacitly assumed.

results.what: A function forced to equal a function with a jump along a curve has Dirichlet integral at least ∫(γ1−γ2)²κ ds/(log(1−κp2)−log(1−κp1)), which tends to infinity as the strip shrinks.
results.modern_name: Lower bound for the Dirichlet energy across a jump (via Cauchy–Schwarz); functions with jump discontinuities are not in H^1.

results.what: A limsup-type jump condition (oscillation bounded below) replacing a minimum-of-jump condition, to cover oscillating discontinuities like sin(1/ρ).

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working draft of material that appears in Riemann's published dissertation on the Dirichlet principle. Only the draft wording and the oscillation refinement add minor detail.

checkable.asserts: The normal integral of dp/(1−κp) equals the logarithmic denominator divided by κ (for 1−κp > 0).
The flat-line limit is p1 − p2.
With p1 = t, p2 = −t, the lower bound tends to infinity as the strip shrinks (m > 0).

transcription_corrections: 'durch k' should be κ (curvature), consistent with the next page.
The sentence should read roughly 'Bezeichnen wir die Krümmung, nach der Seite der positiven p concav als positiv betrachtet, durch κ'.
'C ist also beweisen' should read roughly 'Es ist also zu beweisen, dass ...'.
'Es leuchtet also' is likely 'Es liefert also'.
'gewissenen Stetigkeit der Grenzen willen' is doubtful; possibly 'grösseren Kürze ... willen'.
